headline: Sri Lanka hosts first-ever global summit dedicated to snake science
meta_description: Over 500 researchers from 25 countries gather in Kandy for the inaugural World Congress on Snakes, addressing conservation and the global snakebite crisis.
summary_short: Sri Lanka will host the first international conference entirely dedicated to snakes this October, bringing together 500+ experts to tackle conservation and snakebite res…
body:
Sri Lanka's cultural capital of Kandy will host the inaugural World Congress on Snakes from October 1-4, 2026—a landmark event that marks the first international conference dedicated entirely to snake biology, conservation and public health. More than 400 delegates from 25 countries, including over 300 international scientists and ophiologists, will join more than 100 local researchers at the Grand Kandyan Hotel to address ecological challenges and the global crisis of snakebite envenomation, which kills over 100,000 people annually worldwide. The choice of Sri Lanka as host reflects the island's extraordinary reptilian diversity: it is home to 112 snake species, with more than 63 found nowhere else on Earth.

For decades, snake research has languished on the margins of broader scientific forums. This congress aims to change that by providing the first dedicated, standalone platform for these ecologically vital yet deeply misunderstood reptiles. The four-day event will feature 12 thematic tracks ranging from snake biology and behavior to policies for human coexistence, with particular emphasis on bridging high-level biodiversity science with practical clinical protocols for snakebite management and toxicology. Leading researchers, including advisors from the World Health Organization, will discuss the development of more effective antivenoms.

Beyond laboratories and lecture halls, the congress will take international delegates on field excursions into Sri Lanka's rainforests and dry zones to observe endemic species in their natural habitats. Organizers hope that placing global media attention on this gathering will help advance an agenda of coexistence, moving the conservation narrative from fear and folklore toward science and evidence. By addressing both the ecological crisis facing dwindling snake populations and the human toll of snakebite, the congress aims to demonstrate that protecting snakes and saving human lives are not opposing goals, but interconnected imperatives.
quick_facts: First-ever global conference dedicated entirely to snakes, October 1-4, 2026
Over 500 researchers and conservationists from 25 countries attending in Kandy
Sri Lanka home to 112 snake species, 63+ found nowhere else on Earth
Snakebites kill over 100,000 people annually worldwide, a neglected tropical disease
